# P19: The import’s preview keeps the design rules: Must fix and Check are words with the warning mark, a full outline and no stripe, plain counts, no capsules, no emoji

A check of the core ([the journeys](../journeys.md)): not a journey with steps a person takes, but a script that opens pages and reports what is wrong (Faro’s `evals/finish/18-import-design.cjs`). A rebuild proves the same by hand or with its own script: every failure below must not happen. Each is in the script’s words; {…} is what it measured, and a limit its words don’t give is added after it, in the script’s test (“its test: …”).

## What it checks

P19: the design check on the import's new screens (IM3; docs/design-rules.md). On the preview with a Must fix and a Check: each is a word with the warning mark, never a status shape or a capsule; a Must-fix block is a wash with a full outline, no edge stripe; counts are plain numbers; no emoji.

## Where it looks

- 1280 × 900, as amara, at `/data/import`

A width of 390 is a phone, 1440 (or 1280) a desktop; the address is in the demo on Thursday 5 November 2026 unless it names another day. {…} is a value the script works out as it runs.

## What it reports as wrong

- a block says “{word}”, not Must fix or Check
- the {word} block has no warning mark
- the {word} block's outline is {sides.join('/')}px, not full (its test: `.size > 1`, `x < 1`)
- the {word} block has an edge stripe (its test: `x >= 2`, `.size > 1`)
- a status shape stands for a level
- a capsule on the preview
- a count is drawn as a capsule
- an emoji on the preview
